newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BARCELONA WIN TO FURY OF FIORENTINA FANS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA WIN TO FURY OF FIORENTINA FANS.

text.p: Three-times winners Barcelona reached the European Cup Winners' Cup final on Thursday after a stormy 2-0 win over Fiorentina.
Two Spanish players were hit by objects thrown from the stands as Fiorentina's dreams -- and Italy's hopes of three finalists in the three club competitions -- died.
Barcelona's English coach Bobby Robson said he was hit on the head by a plastic bottle.
Defender Sergi Barjuan received brief medical assistance in the 36th minute when what seemed to be a coin was thrown and Ivan de La Pena was hit in the 65th when taking a throw-in.
On at least two occasions, Swedish referee Anders Frisk consulted a UEFA official on the touchline.

Both teams finished with 10 men, with Fiorentina's Brazilian-born striker Luis Oliveira sent off in the 48th minute for his second bookable offence and Barcelona's Miguel Angel Nadal shown the red card in the 83rd for dangerous play.
"My thoughts were that it was dangerous, that it was becoming violent, maybe never out of control but scary," commented Robson after the 3-1 aggregate victory.
"I thought at one time that if it got worse the referee would stop the match and then what would happen to the result?"
Fiorentina coach Claudio Ranieri was scathing about the referee, saying his actions in holding up play had threatened to turn a containable situation into something worse.
"We cannot condone the crowd's behaviour which was unacceptable," he said. "But if the referee had kept the game flowing it would have been different."

The Fiorentina fans, who have one of the least enviable reputations in Italy as far as behaviour is concerned, were incensed by repeated announcements over the public address system warning that the match could be suspended.
The incidents marred what had started out as a spirited clash between the two former winners of the trophy, welcomed by a roar from the crowd and a barrage of fireworks.
But the contest was killed off when Fernando Couto headed the first goal in the 30th minute following a free kick and Josep Guardiola made it 2-0 five minutes later.
Before that Barcelona's Brazilian ace Ronaldo had rounded goalkeeper Francesco Toldo in the 16th minute and tucked the ball into the net only to be ruled offside.
The decision looked highly debatable.
Ronaldo, the object of huge media attention in Italy following Rome club Lazio's attempts to sign him, was closely marked throughout the match.
Fiorentina, who won the inaugural Cup Winners' Cup in 1961 but have never captured a continental title since then, desperately missed suspended captain Gabriel Batistuta.
"They missed Batistuta," said Robson. "But you must remember that we had four players missing in the first leg."
Portugal's Manuel Rui Costa, Fiorentina captain for the night, hit the post in the 53rd minute from a free kick.
"We defended well after the two goals and Vitor Baia made two important saves," said Robson.
Robson, who has been the target of Barcelona fans for much of the season and is reportedly to be replaced by Ajax coach Louis Van Gaal next season, did not comment on his future.
"I do my work. my work speaks for itself. You draw your own conclusions about it," the former England coach said.
